source: Not every desire is coherent. Therefore some desire is not coherent.

reconstruction.title: Inference from Universal to Existential Statement

evidence.quote: Therefore some desire is not coherent.

translations.reason: The premise 'Not every desire is coherent' is formalized as the negation of the universal statement that all desires are coherent.
The conclusion 'Some desire is not coherent' is formalized as an existential statement asserting the existence of a desire that lacks coherence.

interpretation_notes: The argument relies on the classical first-order equivalence between the negation of a universal statement and the existential statement of its negation.
The domain includes all individuals, with predicates 'Desire' and 'Coherent' restricting the relevant scope without assuming a non-empty subclass of desires.
